questions.def: "Data" is treated as plural in formal contexts.
questions.question: The data ___ inconsistent with the initial hypothesis.

questions.def: Verb agrees with the noun closest to it.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the instructor ___ present.

questions.def: Collective nouns can be singular if acting as one.
questions.question: The ___ has voted to approve the changes.

questions.def: "A number of" is plural, needs plural verb.
questions.question: A number of students ___ absent today.

questions.def: Country names are usually treated as singular.
questions.question: The United States ___ a strong influence globally.

questions.def: Subject names ending in -s are singular.
questions.question: Mathematics are an important subject nowadays.

questions.def: Collective noun treated as a single unit.
questions.question: The ___ is working late tonight.

questions.def: "Neither of" takes a singular verb.
questions.question: Neither of the candidates ___ qualified.

questions.def: Politics is singular when referring to the field.
questions.question: Politics ___ often a contentious topic.

questions.def: Collective noun treated as a single unit.
questions.question: My ___ has decided to move abroad.

questions.def: Diseases ending in -s are singular.
questions.question: Measles ___ a contagious disease.

questions.def: Public treated as a single group.
questions.question: The public ___ demanding better services.

questions.def: Economics is singular, needs singular verb.
questions.question: Economics influence many aspects of our lives.

questions.def: Collective noun treated as a single unit.
questions.question: The ___ is practicing hard for the finals.

questions.def: Jury is single unit.
questions.question: The jury ___ still deliberating the verdict.

questions.def: Amounts of money are singular.
questions.question: Five dollars ___ not enough to buy that.

questions.def: Audience as single unit.
questions.question: The ___ was captivated by the performance.

questions.def: "None of" can be singular.
questions.question: None of the food ___ been eaten.

questions.def: Police is plural.
questions.question: The police ___ investigating the crime.

questions.def: The subject is the singular noun "band", which agrees with "is"; the plural "bands" and the possessives "band's" / "bands'" cannot be the subject here.
questions.question: The ___ is known for their energetic performances.

questions.def: "All that" singular.
questions.question: All that glitters ___ not gold.

questions.def: Each is singular.
questions.question: Each book ___ its own unique story.

questions.def: Cattle is plural.
questions.question: The ___ were grazing peacefully in the field.

questions.def: Few is plural.
questions.question: Few people ___ as generous as him.

questions.def: A pair = singular.
questions.question: A pair of shoes ___ on the floor.

questions.def: 'Data' is often treated as singular in formal/academic contexts.
questions.question: The data ___ that further research is needed.

questions.def: With 'neither/nor,' the verb agrees with the closest noun.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the professor ___ present.

questions.def: Collective nouns like 'board' can be singular.
questions.question: The board ___ themselves by a strict code.

questions.def: 'A number of' is plural; 'the number of' is singular.
questions.question: A number of students ___ absent today.

questions.def: Subjects ending in -ics are usually singular.
questions.question: Mathematics ___ always been a challenging subject.
